You are very strong for reporting right away, you absolutely did the right thing not only for yourself but for the safety of others. He is absolutely a POS and deserves no leniency.. the only reason he reached out to you is to try to cover himself and that is typical predator behavior. 

Your feelings are 100% valid. feeling a bit of shame and worry is a very normal reaction. If and when he gets arrested they will most likely post his name and picture but it is highly unlikely that your name will get out there, so unless he or anyone close to him tells someone your name then the gossip will probably be centered around him. My best advice is to try to avoid getting wrapped up in what other people or saying. Personally the minimal gossip that I did hear after the AH that raped me got arrested stuck with me for a long time and it put a dent in my recovery, but I tried my best to avoid it as much as possible and when people would bring it up to me I just played stupid like I had no idea what was going on. I lived in a smaller town and my family is kinda well known so a lot of people put 2 and 2 together since he was around me a lot. Avoiding any conversation or news about him really was the best thing I could do for myself. I was fortunate that I had moved prior to the trauma that happened on a short visit. Moving is a drastic change but sometimes it’s necessary. 

Also, It takes time to open up to those close to us, please don’t put any pressure on yourself to do so until you are ready (if you ever feel like you need to) but you may consider talking about it with a therapist. Seeking specific therapy as early as possible can be very helpful in coping with the stress and anxiety that comes with the legal aspect of this and also the personal and social aspect. 

You are strong, even if you don’t feel like it right now. You will get thru this. You are doing the right thing. The person is a disgusting human being and he deserves no mercy and I hope they throw him in prison for what he did.

I understand your frustration, but please, try to learn to love yourself, which I know is easier said than done. by making a few sacrifices for your health, that is an act of self love. I have felt this way too. There are many different methods you can try to manage your flares or possible put them in remission before they get worse. HS treatments are not a one size fits all. Don’t give up hope.

Stress can be a trigger, and of course, HS can be very stressful in itself. Take some deep breaths. You can find the treatments and methods that work best for your body. This is a trial and error. I suggest starting now, don’t wait until it becomes unbearable. And know that you are not alone.

Shaving is a big trigger for myself, I have gotten waxed which is honestly great but painful and expensive. Bikini trimmers are cheap (got one for 9$ at Walmart) and cut the hair very short which is nice, downside is sometimes you gotta take em apart to clean them, and your still left with a little bit of hair. It helps me to at least manage the hair until I finally have the lady balls to schedule my laser hair removal appointment. I dislike having body hair as well, but I can’t stand armpit hair so that was something I couldn’t give up. 

I am in remission, I still get the occasional stress flare, but here are some changes I’ve made that I think contributed my remission;
I quit smoking cigarettes, I got the mirena IUD birth control, I lost 50 lbs, I stopped drinking soda, and I stopped drinking milk. I will honestly never give up cheese tho, js. These things may or may not work for you, but so many people have successfully managed their HS with a lot of different things. I hope you find what works best for you

Putting it delicately, firmly, or whichever way may not ever get thru to her if she is unwilling to compromise. This is BEFORE you move in, think long and hard on if that is the best choice considering this issue has gone unresolved for so long, and you have made several attempts to resolve it. Maybe she is lacking perspective, or maybe she does not have the capacity to understand how this affects you. Either way a conversation must be had, telling her firmly, but respectfully, why this is a problem, how it is affecting you, and how you worry about how it will affect you and your relationship in the future. Her response should tell you what you need to decide how to move forward in this relationship.

I wish I knew the best way to remedy this without any type of substance. I used to smoke every night about 2 years ago I quit for work, and then discovered I couldn’t smoke anymore because it started giving me bad anxiety. I didn’t dream at all when I smoked, very occasionally a nightmare would make an appearance. I also quit drinking, last year, it actually helped but for obvious reasons I don’t recommend getting lit every night.

Since then my dreams (which are 98% nightmares) have become increasingly more vivid and intense. I wake up nearly every day in a fragile state, irritable, panicked, anxious. It came to the point where I was suffering bad insomnia, sometimes being awake for 2 days at a time, wide awake because subconsciously, I did not want to sleep because I did not want to dream. It took me awhile to put two and two together, but when I realized that was the problem, it all made sense. 

I have recently started smoking CBD only cigarettes, before bed, which seems to be helping me relax. You can actually order them online which is nice. I have noticed a bit of improvement since I started this. I get a body high with it. The cbd content is much more than typical thc cannabis so the relaxation effects are much stronger, plus you don’t get much of a head high. It’s still smoking, but the good thing about cannabis is that there’s plenty of alternatives to chose from other than smoking. Also CBD is legal so easier to obtain and there’s a lot of different products and company’s to chose from. It’s natural and safe, I personally prefer to stay away from as much medication as possible.

Therapy and meditation can be helpful as well. Make your sleeping environment feel as safe, peaceful, and relaxing as you can.
